---
title: About
---

I am a fourth-year Ph.D. student in Social Psychology at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, where I work with Carol D. Ryff in the Department of Psychology and Institute on Aging. My research centers religion and spirituality, eudaimonic well-being, health, and adult development.

I use large-scale longitudinal data and person-centered methods—including latent profile and latent transition analysis—to understand how patterns of religious and spiritual life relate to psychological and social outcomes across adulthood.

## Education

- Ph.D., Social Psychology (minor: Educational Psychology), University of Wisconsin–Madison, expected 2028
- M.S., Psychology, University of Wisconsin–Madison, 2024
- B.A., Psychology; minor in Philosophy, University of North Carolina Asheville, 2022, *summa cum laude*
